mainTopic: How far an agent (שליח) may stray from his instructions or make mistakes, and the משנה on a court sale whose price was off by a sixth
overview: This amud deals with an agent (שליח) who does not follow his instructions exactly. It opens by finishing an earlier proof: legumes cost the same whether bought in bulk or in small amounts, so buying in parts loses nothing. רב פפא explains that this means a market where each container has a fixed price. A proof from the widow who sold her כתובה property in four separate sales is pushed off, because the land was small, separate plots. The גמרא then asks about an owner who told his agent to sell "to one." רב הונא reads this strictly, while רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא allow even a hundred buyers, and רב נחמן agrees with them. רב נחמן adds that an agent who sold at a wrong price loses his authority: "I sent you to help me, not to harm me." He proves this from תרומה, where an agent's range is narrow but the owner's own act stands. A new משנה then argues about a court sale whose price was off by a sixth. The גמרא opens by asking whether an agent is like the judges or like the widow, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Legumes cost the same in bulk or in small amounts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the earlier proof: legumes have the same price per amount whether bought for a סלע or a פרוטה, so this reading is accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because legumes bought for a סלע and legumes bought for a פרוטה come out at the same price. Learn from here that this is right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is wrapping up a proof from the previous lines. It explains why buying in small parts was not a problem, and then accepts that explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case only works if splitting a purchase loses no money. With legumes, the price per amount does not change with the size of the purchase. So buying bit by bit does not hurt the sender, and the גמרא says 'שמע מינה,' meaning this reading holds.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from this': the point is accepted

phrases.english: For legumes for a sela,
and legumes for a peruta, are the same price.
phrases.notes: Meaning you get the same amount per coin whether you buy a lot or a little.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a proof that began before this section.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Since legumes have one price at any quantity, buying them in small parts does not count as going against instructions.

steps.title: What kind of market has a fixed price for legumes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the case of legumes is. In a market where prices are estimated, a buyer paying a full סלע would get a better deal, so the price would not be the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is a place where they sell by estimating, then when he pays a סלע, the seller gives him a lower price!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the claim from the step before. It shows that in some markets buying in bulk is cheaper, and this sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If sellers estimate the price, a big buyer normally gets a discount. Then buying in small parts would cost more, and the claim that the price stays the same would be wrong. So the גמרא needs a different kind of market for the claim to work.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the case?': asking for the exact situation
'If you say': brings up a possible answer in order to reject it

phrases.english: What are the circumstances?
If you say in a place where they sell by estimation,
then where he gives him a sela,
they lower the price for him more!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי? אִילֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the fixed-price claim the previous step relied on.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what market is the price of legumes the same no matter how much one buys?

steps.title: רב פפא: a market that measures by fixed containers
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the case is a place where legumes are measured in containers at a set price per container.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a place where they measure with containers, and the seller said to him, 'Each container for a פרוטה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question by naming the right kind of market. There, the price per container is fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the deal is 'one container for one פרוטה,' a buyer with a סלע simply gets more containers. He gets no discount for buying more. So buying in small parts loses nothing, and the earlier proof stands.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
In a place where they measure with vessels,
where he said to him: 'Each vessel for a peruta.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: בְּאַתְרָא דְּכָיְילִי בְּכַנֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A market with a fixed price per container, so the amount bought does not change the price.
steps.whatToRemember: The legumes proof only works where each container has a set price, so buying in parts loses nothing.

steps.title: Proof from the widow who sold her husband's property in separate sales
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new proof from the משנה. A widow with a 400-זוז כתובה sold property in four separate sales. Only the last sale, which was underpriced, is cancelled; the first sales stand.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Her כתובה was 400 זוז. She sold to one for a מנה, to another for a מנה, and to the last one property worth a מנה and a דינר for a מנה. The last sale is cancelled, and all the others are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new proof from the משנה about selling in parts. The widow did not sell everything at once, yet her first sales still stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She was entitled to sell property for her full 400 זוז, but she sold one מנה's worth at a time. The משנה only cancels the last sale because it was sold for too little. It does not cancel the earlier sales for being in separate parts, which suggests that splitting a sale is not going against instructions.

keyTerms.meaning: The sum a wife collects when her marriage ends

steps.confusionAlert: The last sale is not cancelled because she sold in parts. It is cancelled because she sold property worth a מנה and a דינר for only a מנה.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If her ketubah was four hundred zuz,
and she sold to this one for a maneh, and to that one for a maneh,
phrases.notes: There are really four buyers here. The third isn't mentioned, but four sales of a מנה add up to the 400.

phrases.english: and to the last one, property worth a maneh and a dinar for a maneh,
the sale of the last one is void,
and as for all the others, their sale is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיְתָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new proof on the same question, now from our משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That selling in parts, when one was authorized to sell more, does not count as going against instructions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the widow with a 400-זוז כתובה who sold in separate sales of a מנה each.

steps.title: The widow's case is about small separate plots
steps.stepSummary: The proof from the widow's four sales is pushed off. That case deals with small, separate plots, so it teaches nothing about an agent who sells less than he was told.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב שישא בריה דרב אידי said about another case, it deals with small plots. Here too, it deals with small plots.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 4. The widow's case is about small, separate pieces of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow's land was made up of small plots that could not be sold as one unit anyway. So selling them one at a time was the natural way to sell. This tells us nothing about an agent who chooses to sell less than he was told.

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי,
phrases.english: As Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said
it is about small plots;
phrases.notes: These are small fields spread out in different places, not one big field.

phrases.english: here too, it is about small plots.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּדְאָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the widow who sold in four sales
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The case is about small separate plots that had to be sold one at a time, so it is not a case of an agent choosing to sell less.

steps.title: An owner tells his agent to sell "to one" without saying more
steps.stepSummary: If the owner clearly said "to one and not to two," selling to two obviously breaks his instructions. The question is what happens when he only said "to one."
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious that if he said "to one and not to two," the agent may not sell to two, because the owner said so outright. But if he just said "to one," what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. It first states the obvious case, then asks about the unclear case where the owner only said "to one."
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the owner adds "not to two," an agent who sells to two has plainly gone against him. When the owner only says "to one," we do not know whether he was setting a limit or just speaking in a normal way. That unclear case is what the גמרא wants to know.

keyTerms.meaning: To one and not to two

phrases.english: It is obvious: if he said, "Sell to one, and not to two,"
phrases.notes: The owner is speaking to his agent about selling his land.

phrases.english: then he told him outright, "to one and not to two."
If he told him just "to one," without saying more, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא, אָמַר לְאֶחָד וְלֹא לִשְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about an agent's instructions
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether "to one" said by itself stops the agent from selling to two people

steps.title: רב הונא: "to one" means only one
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that "to one" sets a limit. The agent may not sell to two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: "To one" means to one, and not to two.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives the first answer. He reads "to one" as a strict limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב הונא, the owner's words count exactly as he said them. Saying "to one" is the same as saying "not to two."

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
"To one" means to one, and not to two.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "To one" means only one buyer, so selling to two goes against the instructions.

steps.title: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא: even to a hundred
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא disagree with רב הונא. In their view, "to one" does not stop the agent from selling to two, or even to a hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא both say: "To one" even allows two. "To one" even allows a hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion argues with רב הונא. Here "to one" is not treated as a limit at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their view, the owner was just speaking in a normal way and did not mean one buyer only. So the agent may divide the sale among many buyers.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה בר רב הונא is רב הונא's son, yet here he disagrees with his father.

phrases.aramaic: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna both say:
"To one" means even to two.
"To one" means even to a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב הונא in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "To one" is not a limit, so the agent may sell to two people or even to a hundred.

steps.title: The question is brought to רב נחמן in סורא
steps.stepSummary: When רב נחמן visits סורא, רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא ask him how to rule in this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן came to סורא. רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא went in to him and asked: In a case like this, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short story that sets up the next step. The question is brought to a senior authority, and his answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same argument from steps 7 and 8 is now put before רב נחמן. His answer will decide between the two opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: סורא, a major Torah center in Babylonia

phrases.english: Rav Nachman happened to come to Sura.

phrases.aramaic: עוּל לְגַבֵּיהּ רַב חִסְדָּא וְרַבָּה בַּר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Chisda and Rabba bar Rav Huna went in to him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא מַאי?
phrases.english: They said to him: In a case like this, what is the law?
phrases.notes: "A case like this" means the owner who just said "to one" from step 6.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיקְּלַע רַב נַחְמָן לְסוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the argument to רב נחמן to settle it
steps.sheelahInformationSought: רב נחמן's ruling on an owner who just said "to one"

steps.title: רב נחמן: even to two, even to a hundred
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן agrees with רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא. "To one" allows selling to two, and even to a hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: "To one" even allows two. "To one" even allows a hundred.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers and sides with the lenient view. Plain "to one" does not hold back the agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן repeats the exact words of רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, so his authority supports their view against רב הונא. Only clear words like "not to two" would stop the agent from selling to more than one buyer.
steps.whatToRemember: If an owner says "sell to one" and nothing more, the agent may sell to two or more buyers. Only "to one and not to two" limits him. רב נחמן agrees with רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא.

phrases.english: He said to them: "To one" means even to two;
"To one" means even to a hundred.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: לְאֶחָד וַאֲפִילּוּ לִשְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 and settles the argument
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Plain "to one" lets the agent sell to many buyers, following רב נחמן, רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא.

steps.title: Does the sale stand even if the agent made a mistake?
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא ask רב נחמן whether his ruling applies even when the agent erred in the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: Even if the agent made a mistake?
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן's questioners ask a follow-up about his ruling. Does it still hold if the agent made a mistake, such as selling for too little?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן allowed the agent to sell to more than one buyer. Now they test how far that ruling goes. Is the agent's sale valid even when he got the price wrong?

keyTerms.meaning: Agent, someone sent to act for another person

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: "They" are רב חסדא and רבה בר רב הונא, speaking to רב נחמן.

phrases.english: Even though the agent made a mistake?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אַף עַל גַּב דִּטְעָה שָׁלִיחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far רב נחמן's ruling in Step 10 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the agent's sale is valid even when he made a pricing mistake.

steps.title: Not when the agent made a mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that his ruling does not cover a case where the agent erred.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: I did not say my ruling about a case where the agent made a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן limits his own ruling. If the agent made a mistake, the sale does not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling to two buyers is allowed, but selling badly is not. The agent's authority covers selling, not a mistaken sale that harms the owner.

phrases.english: He said to them:
Where the agent made a mistake, I did not say so.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לְהוּ: דִּטְעָה שָׁלִיחַ לָא קָאָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An agent who erred does not have a valid sale; רב נחמן's ruling does not cover that case.

steps.title: But there is no price-cheating rule for land
steps.stepSummary: They challenge רב נחמן from his own rule that אונאה does not apply to land.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: But didn't the master say there is no אונאה for land?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioners challenge רב נחמן with his own earlier rule. Land sales are not undone because of a wrong price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a wrong price never cancels a land sale, then the agent's mistake should not matter either. So why should his sale be undone?

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't the master say? (introduces a challenge from his own words)
Overcharging or underpaying, which can undo a sale

phrases.english: They said to him: But didn't the master say
There is no price-fraud claim for land!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר מָר אֵין אוֹנָאָה לְקַרְקָעוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's claim that an agent's pricing mistake cancels the sale.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since land has no אונאה, a wrong price should never cancel a land sale, even one made by an agent.

steps.title: An owner's mistake is different from an agent's mistake
steps.stepSummary: The rule of no אונאה for land applies only when the owner himself erred. If the agent erred, the owner can say, 'I sent you to help me, not to harm me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: That rule applies only when the owner made the mistake. But if the agent made the mistake, the owner can tell him: I sent you to improve things for me, not to damage them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the challenge. He separates an owner's mistake from an agent's mistake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of no אונאה for land means a sale stands even at a bad price. That holds when the owner sold it himself. An agent only has authority to act for the owner's benefit, so a harmful mistake falls outside his job, and the sale is not valid.

keyTerms.meaning: I sent you to fix things for me, not to ruin them

steps.whatToRemember: An agent is appointed only to benefit the sender. If he causes harm, he has gone beyond what he was sent to do, even where the same act by the owner would stand.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of agency (שליחות). An agent's authority is limited to acting for the sender's good.

phrases.aramaic: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דִּטְעָה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: This applies only where the owner made the mistake,
but if the agent made the mistake, he can say to him:
"I sent you to improve things for me, not to damage them."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי הֵיכָא דִּטְעָה בַּעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the rule: no אונאה for land applies only to the owner's own mistake.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: No אונאה for land means every land sale stands, no matter who made the mistake.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only an owner who erred. An agent who erred was acting outside his mission, so the sale is cancelled.

steps.title: What is the source for treating an agent differently?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that an agent's mistake is treated differently from an owner's mistake.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do you know that there is a difference between an agent and an owner?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב נחמן's distinction. This line sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן's answer depends on agents and owners being treated differently. The גמרא now wants an earlier source that shows this difference.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say (this)? A request for a source

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that there is a difference between an agent and an owner?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּשָׁאנֵי בֵּין שָׁלִיחַ לְבַעַל הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source behind the distinction made in Step 14.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that an agent's mistake is treated differently from an owner's mistake.

steps.title: A משנה about an agent sent to separate תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins quoting a משנה. An agent sent to separate תרומה follows the owner's wishes. If he doesn't know them, he gives one-fiftieth, and anything from one-fortieth to one-sixtieth still counts as תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: If someone tells his agent, 'Go and separate תרומה,' the agent separates according to the owner's wishes. If he doesn't know the owner's wishes, he separates a middle amount, one-fiftieth. If he went ten lower or ten higher, his תרומה is valid תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts bringing its proof from a משנה about an agent separating תרומה. This part lays out the basic rules for the agent, and the comparison to the owner is being built up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no fixed amount for תרומה, so the agent must follow what the owner would want. The agent is tied to the owner's wishes, and he has a set range when he doesn't know them. This sets up how an agent's mistakes will be judged differently from an owner's.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: As we learned: One who says to his agent, "Go out and separate תרומה" —
he separates according to the owner's wishes.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ דַּעְתּוֹ שֶׁל בַּעַל הַבַּיִת —
phrases.english: And if he does not know the owner's wishes —
he separates a middle amount, one out of fifty,
if he went down ten or up ten —
phrases.notes: Ten is taken off or added to the fifty, so one out of forty or one out of sixty.

phrases.english: his תרומה is valid תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הָאוֹמֵר לִשְׁלוּחוֹ צֵא וּתְרוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the request for a source in Step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That an agent's actions are judged differently from an owner's actions.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in תרומות 4:4 about an agent sent to separate תרומה.

steps.title: The owner's תרומה counts even at one-twentieth
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when the owner himself separates even one-twentieth as תרומה, it still counts. That completes the proof that an agent's mistake is treated differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: But about the owner himself a ברייתא teaches: if he separated תרומה and even one-twentieth came up in his hand, his תרומה is valid תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof it began in step 16. It sets the agent's limits next to the owner's much wider freedom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An agent's separation only works between one-fortieth and one-sixtieth. If the owner himself takes off as much as one-twentieth, it is still valid. So the same mistake works when the owner makes it but fails when an agent makes it. That is exactly the difference between an owner and a שליח that רב נחמן relied on.
steps.whatToRemember: An agent who goes outside the owner's wishes accomplishes nothing: 'I sent you to help me, not to harm me.' The owner's own act stands even when it is unusual.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proves the principle from step 14. An agent's mistake can cancel a transaction even in areas where the owner's own mistake would not.

phrases.english: Whereas regarding the homeowner himself it is taught:
If he separated תרומה and there came up in his hand
phrases.notes: Meaning: the amount he actually took off turned out to be this much, even though he didn't plan it.

phrases.english: even one-twentieth
his תרומה is valid תרומה.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ גַּבֵּי בַּעַל הַבַּיִת תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the contrast begun in the משנה quoted in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: An agent's mistake is treated differently from the owner's own mistake.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the owner's separation of even one-twentieth is valid. Compare the agent's narrow range in the משנה.

steps.title: Proof from the widow who sold in several sales
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from a משנה that a person does not mind having extra sale documents. A widow sold her property in separate sales, and those sales are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: if her כתובה was four hundred זוז, and she sold to one person for a מנה, to another for a מנה, and to the last one something worth a מנה and a דינר for a מנה, the last sale is void, and all the other sales stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier question: does a person mind having more documents than necessary out against him? It brings a משנה as a possible proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The widow could have sold everything in one sale. Instead she made several sales, and each sale creates another document the orphans must worry about. Yet the משנה says the earlier sales are valid. That would suggest the orphans cannot object to extra documents. Only the last sale, priced below its value, is void.

keyTerms.meaning: Her כתובה, the amount owed to her from her husband's estate

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two parts. The last sale is void because of its wrong price. The proof comes from the earlier sales, which stay valid even though she split them up.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If her כתובה was four hundred zuz,
and she sold to this one for a maneh,
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred זוז, so four sales would add up to her four hundred.

phrases.english: and to that one for a maneh,
and to the last one, property worth a maneh and a dinar, for a maneh,
the sale of the last one is void,
and as for all the others, their sale stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָיְתָה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ אַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת זוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the agent discussion and returns to the question of whether a person minds extra documents.
steps.raayaObject: A person does not mind having multiple documents out against him.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of the widow who sold her כתובה property in separate sales, which are valid.

steps.title: The sales were of small, separate plots
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי rejects the proof. The משנה is speaking about small, scattered plots that could not be sold as one unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: it is speaking about small plots.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא pushes back on the proof from step 18. He explains the case so that it no longer proves anything about extra documents.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the property was made up of small, separate pieces, the widow could not have sold it in one sale. Splitting it up was necessary, not her choice. So the משנה says nothing about whether owners mind unnecessary extra documents.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
It is speaking of small plots.
phrases.notes: Small, scattered pieces of land that could not be sold together, so separate sales were unavoidable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: בְּקַטִּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 18.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely, by limiting the case in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed she chose to split the sales. With small separate plots, splitting was forced on her.

steps.title: New משנה: judges' assessment off by a sixth
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that if the judges' assessment of a property was too low or too high by a sixth, the sale is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: When the judges assessed a property and went below its value by a sixth, or above it by a sixth, their sale is void.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It sets a rule for property that בית דין sells based on its own price assessment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Judges sometimes sell property, for example to pay a debt or a כתובה, at a price they assess. If their price is off from the real value by a full sixth in either direction, the sale does not stand at all. The mistake cancels the sale; it is not just fixed by paying back the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: They decreased (set the price too low)

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new discussion of when a mistaken sale by בית דין is cancelled. It ties back to the earlier theme of an agent's mistakes.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
The assessment of the judges
that went below the value by a sixth
or added a sixth above it
their sale is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּם הַדַּיָּינִין שֶׁפִּיחֲתוּ שְׁתוּת אוֹ הוֹסִיפוּ שְׁתוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale by the judges whose assessment was off by a sixth, too low or too high, is void.

steps.title: The Court's Sale Stays Valid
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל disagrees with the first opinion and rules that the judges' sale is valid even with a mistake of a sixth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: their sale is valid. If it were void, what extra power would בית דין have?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second opinion. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the judges' sale stands even though their price was off by a sixth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in step 20 said a mistake of a sixth cancels the sale. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argues that the court must have more power than a regular seller. If a court sale could be canceled like anyone else's, the court's authority would mean nothing special.

keyTerms.meaning: Their sale is valid and stands
The power and authority of the court
If so; if that were true

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the idea that a court's actions carry extra strength. The coming question about an agent depends on this.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Their sale is valid.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן — מָה כֹּחַ בֵּית דִּין יָפֶה?
phrases.english: If so, what advantage is there to the power of the court?
phrases.notes: He means: if the court's sale could be canceled for this mistake, the court would be no stronger than an ordinary seller.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: מִכְרָן קַיָּים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a disagreeing opinion to the first ruling of the משנה in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale made by the court stays valid even if the price was off by a sixth, because the court has special authority.

steps.title: A Publicly Announced Sale Always Stands
steps.stepSummary: If the court announced the sale publicly, the sale is valid even if the price was badly off, at double or half the value.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if they made a public notice for inspection, then even if they sold something worth 100 for 200, or worth 200 for 100, their sale is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a case everyone agrees on. If the sale was publicly announced, it stands no matter how wrong the price turned out to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 20 and 21 argued about a court sale with no announcement. Here the court let the public come, look at the field and bid. Since the sale was open to everyone, the price that buyers offered counts as fair, even if it was double or half the value.

keyTerms.meaning: A public notice inviting people to come inspect the property and bid
A sum of one hundred דינרים

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this case is part of the argument. Even the first opinion agrees that a publicly announced sale stands, even with a huge price gap.
steps.whatToRemember: No announcement: the first opinion says a mistake of a sixth cancels the sale, and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the sale stands. With a public announcement, the sale always stands.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִם עָשׂוּ אִגֶּרֶת בִּקּוֹרֶת בֵּינֵיהֶן,
phrases.english: But if they made a document of inspection among them,
phrases.notes: This is a public announcement telling people to come look at the field and make offers.

phrases.english: even if they sold something worth one hundred for two hundred
or something worth two hundred for one hundred,
their sale is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל אִם עָשׂוּ אִגֶּרֶת בִּקּוֹרֶת בֵּינֵיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the case of a publicly announced sale, where the sale stands no matter how far off the price was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court sale made after a public announcement is valid even if the price was double or half the true value.

steps.title: Is an Agent Like the Judges or Like the Widow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether an agent who sold at a wrong price is treated like the judges, whose sale stands for a small mistake, or like the widow, whose sale is canceled.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A question was asked: an agent, who is he like?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a question. It asks how to treat a שליח who sells property at the wrong price.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two models. Judges have a margin, so a small mistake does not cancel their sale. The widow selling on her own has no such margin, and any mistake cancels it. The גמרא wants to know which model fits an agent, who sells for someone else like judges do but has no court authority.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A question was raised before the scholars
An agent acting on behalf of another person
Like whom? Which case does he match?

steps.whyThisMatters: This question decides whether anyone who sells for others gets the judges' margin, or only a real court does.

phrases.english: Gemara: A dilemma was raised before them:
An agent, who is he like?
phrases.notes: Is he like the judges from the משנה, or like the widow, whose sale is canceled for any mistake?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: שָׁלִיחַ, כְּמַאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה ends, the גמרא opens its discussion by asking where an agent fits between the judges and the widow.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether an agent who sells at the wrong price has the judges' margin of a sixth, or whether his sale is canceled for any mistake, like the widow's.
